question: Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia responds well to amoxicillin because the organism possesses a cell wall with abundant peptidoglycan.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Mycoplasma pneumoniae is unique among bacterial pathogens because it has NO cell wall at all. Since beta-lactams like amoxicillin work by inhibiting peptidoglycan synthesis, they are completely ineffective. Treat with macrolides (azithromycin) or fluoroquinolones (levofloxacin).
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — the statement is false. Mycoplasma pneumoniae completely LACKS a cell wall, making all beta-lactam antibiotics (which target peptidoglycan synthesis) ineffective. Macrolides such as azithromycin or fluoroquinolones such as levofloxacin are the drugs of choice for atypical pneumonia.
